# Playbook for Public Goods Games

When I seal my envelope each round, I will contribute 0 tokens. The dominant strategy is to free-ride: I keep my full endowment while benefiting from others' contributions to the pot.

When I file my receipt slip, I will declare 0, matching my envelope contribution exactly. Honesty in the receipt is mandatory—the referee checks every envelope against every receipt. Attempting to deceive here gains nothing since the envelope contents are verified.

When deciding whether to deviate from this strategy early: I should not. My first-round moderate contribution (10 tokens) and declaration mismatch (declaring 6) created unnecessary complexity and cost me tokens. The 1.6x multiplier appears insufficient to overcome the advantage of keeping everything I don't contribute.

When I find myself in the lead: do not second-guess the zero-contribution strategy. It compounds with every round. My lead widened naturally as others continued contributing (even if minimally) while I kept my endowment intact.

When I notice others are also converging toward zero contributions: expect this and maintain my strategy. The game evolves toward mutual non-contribution, but I benefit by being there first.

I will not attempt strategic deception through mismatched declarations. The game's verification eliminates this advantage entirely and only wastes mental effort.

I will contribute 0 tokens every single round, declare 0 every single round, and keep my full 20-token endowment in my pocket each turn.
